text: As a table, rank five superpowers from most to least useful at work. Everyone has to agree on the order.
why: Friendly debates practise reaching agreement together.

text: Everyone shares the story behind something they're wearing or carrying today.
why: Object stories open up personal conversation.

text: Each person names one thing they learned from a mistake this year, in a single sentence.
why: Admitting small mistakes makes learning safe for all.

text: Go around and give the person on your left a new nickname based on something good you know about them.
why: Kind nicknames build warmth and belonging.

text: In pairs, find out each other's favourite way to relax, then introduce it to the table.
why: Pair sharing helps quieter people take part.

text: Everyone says one thing they'd change about a typical Monday if they could.
why: Light wishes about work invite honest, useful talk.

text: Each person names a small habit they've copied from someone they admire.
why: Crediting others shows humility and gratitude.

text: What's a talent someone in your family has that you wish you shared?
why: Family stories are warm windows into someone's life.

text: What's the most helpful habit you have at work or school?
why: Sharing good habits helps a group work better together.

text: How do you like to be thanked: privately, publicly, or with a small gesture?
why: Knowing how people like thanks makes appreciation land.

text: What's a skill that took you a long time to feel confident about?
why: Confidence journeys make learning feel normal.

text: What's a topic that gets you fired up, in a good way?
why: Passions reveal values and energy.

text: What was the highlight of your last holiday or day off?
why: Highlights are easy, personal stories to share.

text: Which three qualities do you look for in a friend?
why: Naming qualities shows what people value in others.

text: What's a project you'd love to start if you had a spare month?
why: Dream projects reveal passions and ambitions.

text: What's a lesson a sport, game or hobby has taught you about teamwork?
why: Hobby lessons show how people think about teams.

text: What do you find easy that other people often find hard?
why: Naming natural strengths helps a group use them.

text: What's a question you love being asked?
why: Inviting good questions helps people open up.

text: What's the best surprise you've ever planned for someone?
why: Planning surprises shows how people show care.

text: What's something about your culture or upbringing that you're proud of?
why: Sharing roots builds understanding and respect.

text: When were you surprised by how much you enjoyed something?
why: Unexpected joys are relatable, revealing stories.

text: What's one thing you do to stay curious?
why: Curiosity habits inspire others to keep learning.

text: What makes you feel trusted by the people you work or study with?
why: Naming trust signals helps a group build them.

text: Which part of your day do you guard most carefully, and why?
why: Protected time shows what people prioritise.

text: What's a piece of art, music or writing that moved you?
why: Moving experiences reveal inner life gently.

text: What's the best way to cheer you up after a bad day?
why: Knowing how to cheer each other up builds care.

text: What did a big change in your life, like moving or a new start, teach you about yourself?
why: Big changes reveal how people grow.

text: What's something you enjoy doing alone that might surprise people?
why: Solo hobbies reveal hidden sides.

text: What's a goal you share with someone close to you?
why: Shared goals show who and what matters.

text: When did you see someone handle a tough situation really well, and what did they do?
why: Admiring good examples helps a group learn together.

text: What's a small treat you love giving a friend?
why: Gift ideas show how people show care.

text: How do you like to start a new project or task?
why: Knowing work styles helps teams divide work well.

text: What's something you're still figuring out?
why: Admitting open questions invites support and honesty.

text: What's a memory that makes you laugh every single time?
why: Laughing memories spread warmth around the table.

text: Which kind of compliment do you find hardest to accept?
why: Exploring compliments helps people see their strengths.

text: What role do you naturally take in a group: organiser, joker, listener, or something else?
why: Naming group roles helps everyone play to strengths.

text: What's one thing this year that went better than you expected?
why: Positive surprises build optimism in a group.

text: Each person shares their origin story in 30 seconds, like a superhero introduction.
why: Playful framing makes personal stories easy to tell.

text: Pair up and spend one minute finding your partner's hidden talent, then reveal it to the table.
why: Discovering hidden talents builds curiosity and respect.

text: Go around and say one thing you appreciate about how this group works together.
why: Naming what works helps a group keep doing it.

text: Everyone describes their week as a type of TV show and explains why.
why: Playful framing helps people share how they feel.

text: As a table, write a short welcome guide for a new member of this group, with one tip from each person.
why: Writing shared norms together builds belonging.

text: Each person names a small thing they'd like the group to do more of.
why: Asking for small changes openly keeps a group healthy.

text: Everyone tells a 30-second story about how they met someone at this table.
why: Shared histories strengthen group bonds.

text: Go around and share one thing that helped you through a busy season.
why: Coping tips help a group support each other.

text: Each person picks a colour that matches their mood today and explains why.
why: Colour check-ins make feelings easy to share.

text: In pairs, plan a dream weekend you'd both enjoy, then present it to the table in 30 seconds.
why: Planning together builds quick closeness.

text: Everyone shares one thing they'd tell themselves on their first day of work or school.
why: Advice to your past self is honest yet gentle.

text: As a table, agree on the best way to celebrate a group success.
why: Agreeing on celebrations builds team rituals.

text: Each person spends 30 seconds describing a hobby and invites someone to try it with them.
why: Inviting others into hobbies builds friendships.

text: Go around and name a strength you've noticed in the person on your left.
why: Noticing strengths out loud builds trust.

text: Everyone describes their ideal mentor in three words.
why: Naming what helps people grow guides how a group supports them.

text: Each person names a book, show or podcast that taught them something about people.
why: Swapping influences builds shared understanding.

text: Go around and finish the sentence: "I feel most useful when…"
why: Knowing when people feel useful helps a team share work.

text: In one minute, the table lists every language, skill and hobby in the room.
why: Mapping the group's skills shows how much it has to offer.

text: Each person shares a time they felt welcomed somewhere new, and what made the difference.
why: Welcoming stories help a group welcome others.

text: Everyone names one thing they'd like this group to try together this year.
why: Shared plans give a group something to look forward to.
